Your robot arm’s first pick.

You are an automation engineer setting up a workstation on a small assembly line. A blue component arrives in the Pickup area, and your job is to plan how the robot will place it in the Target tray without dropping it or hitting nearby objects.

Explore the joints and coordinate frames, then arrange the pick-and-place steps before programming a physical robot.

    Start with a real problem. Learn to transfer knowledge.

    How a learning scenario is organised

    Understand the task, explore the model, connect concepts and experiment. Then explain your choices using what you observed.

    Understand the problem

    Define the real context, learners, prior knowledge and evidence of success.

    Explore and ask

    Explore key objects through 3D, images or video, with Tutor explanations connected to the selected part.

    Connect and practise

    Use the knowledge map to see relationships, then test your understanding through small tasks.

    Explain and transfer

    Discuss what changed and consider how the principles apply to another device or discipline.

    A teaching showcase you can build on.

    Features, sources and future integration

    Interactive 3D in the browser

    An original simplified arm built with Three.js supports orbiting, zooming, multiple views, part selection and joint-angle demonstrations. It is not an exact UR5 model and does not solve inverse kinematics, dynamics or collision detection.

    Tutor demo and AI integration

    The demo uses local rules and a scenario knowledge base, with no live AI model. A future server can pass questions, the selected part and scenario knowledge to the institution’s chosen model. API credentials should remain on that server.

    A reusable learning structure

    Reuse the scenario description, media, concepts, Tutor context, tasks and industry opportunities with a case from another discipline. The template form exports JSON.

    Real logo sources

    Universal Robots and ABB logos come from their official websites. The China Mobile mark comes from a China Mobile Hong Kong press asset. UR source · ABB source · CMHK press source. Logos are not endorsements.

    References and licences

    The learning structure draws on TU Delft’s DigiPedia UR5 course and HANDZONe. This page uses original teaching content and a simplified model; no institutional endorsement is implied. Three.js r160.1 is included under the MIT License, with the full licence embedded in this HTML.
